rows.ARS:
Yellow blend Floribunda.
Registration name: HARsherry
Exhibition name: Sheila's Perfume
rows.Origin:
Bred by John Sheridan (United Kingdom, before 1979).
Introduced in United Kingdom by R Harkness & Co. Ltd. in 1985 as 'Sheila's Perfume'.
rows.Bloom: Yellow blend, red edges. Strong fragrance. 20 to 25 petals. Average diameter 4.5". Large, double (17-25 petals), borne mostly solitary, high-centered bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Medium, bushy. Medium, semi-glossy, dark green foliage.

Height: 30" to 6' (75 to 185cm). Width: 2' to 4' (60 to 120cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 6b through 10b. Can be used for beds and borders, container rose, cut flower or garden. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) . Can be grown in the ground or in a container (container requires winter protection).
